A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STITCH-OPE study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–N are readable and can be matched despite added material and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original GaussianWorld simulations, D4RL and Gym OPE evaluations, diffusion-policy experiments, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Hopper experiments covering behavior datasets, evaluation horizons, reward estimation, and a further diffusion baseline.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain conditional sub-trajectory diffusion, negative behavior guidance, trajectory stitching, and reward prediction. Expanded architecture documentation does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix L.3 adds Hopper-medium-expert and Hopper-expert, extending coverage to mixed and expert behavior-data distributions. The environments, control tasks, and target-policy families otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 17 newly evaluates Ding et al.'s Diffusion World Model against PGD and STITCH-OPE on Hopper-medium. Comparator membership in the original Tables 2–3 is retained.

E3.justification: The new horizon experiment tests T = 128, 256, 512, 768, and 1000 with gamma = 0.999 and normalization shared across horizons. Appendix L.4 adds a true-reward control. These are localized additional protocols; the original benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's guidance-coefficient and window-size sweeps and trajectory visualizations, v2 adds tests of evaluation-horizon sensitivity, robustness to behavior-data quality, and accumulated reward-estimation error. These substantially expand the questions examined by controlled and robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and error bars of one standard error in Section 4.1 and Appendix I. The added comparisons continue this practice without introducing new uncertainty estimation or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes FQE's Hopper Regret@1 from 0.13 ± 0.03 to 0.34 ± 0.03; Table 3 is unchanged. Tables 4 and 13–17 add substantial horizon, dataset, reward-control, and DWM results. The horizon scores use different discounting and normalization, so they are additional evaluations rather than same-setting improvements over Table 2.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3, its assumptions, and the entropy and bias–variance proofs in Appendices C–D are retained. Apparent equation differences from extraction are formatting differences, not revised mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning stitching, negative behavior guidance, theoretical error reduction, and robust long-horizon OPE. The new experiments provide additional support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new tests as evidence of robustness across behavior distributions, limited reward-estimation effects, and favorable horizon dependence. Appendix L.6 adds an explanation linking DWM's limitations to its handling of actions and policy guidance. Section 5's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix J newly specifies six residual blocks, their convolution/normalization/activation structure, time embedding, and 256 denoising steps. v2 also adds a project/code pointer and a checklist statement about supplementary code and a README. These expand documentation without demonstrating implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ding et al.'s Diffusion World Model citation and discusses its relationship to STITCH-OPE in Appendices L.6 and N. Existing related work is largely retained; splitting and renumbering the bibliography does not represent removal of those works.

P1.justification: Section 4.4 becomes a structured summary, several appendix passages gain descriptive headings, a NeurIPS checklist is inserted, and references are split between the main paper and supplement. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact, with additional byline and conference-header edits.

P2.justification: New tables display horizon sensitivity, two behavior-dataset comparisons, aggregate and per-policy reward controls, and DWM results. The hyperparameter table gains a denoising-step row, while Table 3 and several figures are repositioned or resized. This substantially expands tabular presentation while retaining the original figures' content.

improvement.justification: The horizon, behavior-data, and reward-control experiments directly test claims that v1 supported less thoroughly, while Appendix J and the code pointer improve reproducibility documentation. The gains are incremental and concentrated on Hopper. Some superiority language exceeds the displayed evidence, including Table 13's Regret@1 tie within the claimed five-of-six wins.
